title: CORPRES: A Fully Annotated Corpus of Russian Speech
why_promising: Primary Russian production corpus from 8 speakers (4 female, 4 male), 60 hours total / 528458 running words. Six annotation levels include pitch marks, phonetic events, narrow and wide phonetic transcription, orthographic transcription, and prosodic transcription. The paper states that 40% of the corpus was manually segmented and fully annotated on all six levels, spanning all speakers and speaking styles. This manual subset is strongly eligible in principle and could contribute segmental, landmark, transcription, pitch/prosody, and style-linked production data.
open_question: Do not admit until an authoritative publicly accessible deposit or licensed research distribution is resolved and the manually segmented 40% can be isolated from the partly/automatically annotated remainder. Enumerate actual files, license, annotation format, speaker/style identifiers, and manual-versus-generated provenance before core ingestion.
